citation.title: Unbiased Estimation of the Average Treatment Effect in Cluster-Randomized Experiments

standing_assumptions:
Finite-population, design-based potential-outcomes setting; the only randomness is the allocation of clusters. Transcribed from the page images.

(S1) p. 41 (PDF p. 3), Section 2: 'Define treatment indicator $D_i\in\{0,1\}$ for units $i\in 1,2,\ldots,N$ such that $D_i=1$ when unit $i$ receives the treatment and $D_i=0$ otherwise. Assuming that the stable unit treatment value assumption (Rubin 1978, 2005) holds, let $Y_{1i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is exposed to the treatment, and let $Y_{0i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is not exposed to the treatment. The observed experimental outcome $Y_i$ may be expressed as a function of the potential outcomes and the assigned treatment: $Y_i=D_iY_{1i}+(1-D_i)Y_{0i}$. The causal effect of the treatment on unit $i$, $\tau_i$, is defined as the difference between the two potential outcomes for unit $i$: $\tau_i\equiv Y_{1i}-Y_{0i}$. And, by definition the ATE, denoted $\Delta$, is the average value of $\tau_i$ for all units $i$. Under this model, the only random component of the experiment is the allocation of units to treatment and control groups.' Then $\Delta=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^N(Y_{1i}-Y_{0i})}{N}=\frac1N\left[\sum_{i=1}^NY_{1i}-\sum_{i=1}^NY_{0i}\right]=\frac1N[Y_1^T-Y_0^T]$, 'where $Y_1^T$ is the sum of potential outcomes if in the treatment condition and $Y_0^T$ is the sum of potential outcomes if in the control condition', and equation (1): $\hat\Delta=\frac1N\left[\widehat{Y_1^T}-\widehat{Y_0^T}\right]$.

(S2) p. 42 (PDF p. 4), Section 2: 'Formally, the bias of an estimator is the difference between the expected value of the estimator (over all randomizations) and the parameter of interest. If the estimators $\widehat{Y_0^T}$ and $\widehat{Y_1^T}$ are unbiased, the corresponding estimator of $\Delta$ is also unbiased since $\mathrm{E}[\hat\Delta]=\frac1N\left[\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{Y_1^T}\right]-\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{Y_0^T}\right]\right]=\frac1N[Y_1^T-Y_0^T]=\Delta$.' Footnote 3: 'Throughout, we use the term random allocation to refer to the assignment of a fixed number of units (or clusters) to treatment and a fixed number to control, following the terminology of Lachin (1988).'

(S3) p. 44 (PDF p. 6), Section 3.2 (the cluster design every result below inherits): 'Formally, suppose each cluster $j=1,2,\ldots,M$ is assigned to either treatment or control. Define $m_t$ and $M$ as (fixed) integers such that $0<m_t<M$. Now $m_t$ clusters are randomly assigned to treatment ($D_j=1$) and the remaining $m_c=M-m_t$ clusters are assigned to control ($D_j=0$). Define $J_0$ as the set of all $j$ such that $D_j=0$ and $J_1$ as the set of all $j$ such that $D_j=1$. Let $Y_{0ij}$ be the response of the $i^{th}$ individual in the $j^{th}$ cluster if the cluster is assigned to control and let $Y_{1ij}$ be the response of the $i^{th}$ individual in the $j^{th}$ cluster if the cluster is assigned to treatment. Let $n_j$ be the number of individuals in the $j^{th}$ cluster. Note that all individuals have the same probability $m_t/M$ of entering treatment.' Also p. 44: '$n_t=\sum_{j\in J_1}n_j$ and $n_c=\sum_{j\in J_0}n_j$ are no longer fixed numbers ... but are now random variables.'

(S4) p. 48 (PDF p. 10), Section 4 (cluster totals): 'Define $Y^T_{0j}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}Y_{0ij}$ as the sum of responses of the individuals in the $j^{th}$ cluster if assigned to control and $Y^T_{1j}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}Y_{1ij}$ as the sum of responses of the individuals in the $j^{th}$ cluster if assigned to treatment. ... The observed cluster total for cluster $j$, $Y^T_j$, may be expressed as: $Y^T_j=D_jY^T_{1j}+(1-D_j)Y^T_{0j}$.' and '$\Delta=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^M\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}(Y_{1ij}-Y_{0ij})}{\sum_{j=1}^M\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}1}=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^MY^T_{1j}-\sum_{j=1}^MY^T_{0j}}{\sum_{j=1}^Mn_j}=\frac1N[Y^T_1-Y^T_0]$.'

(S5) p. 50 (PDF p. 12), Section 4.2 (finite population moments, divisor $M$): 'given features $v_j$ and $w_j$ for $j\in 1,\ldots,M$, finite population variance $\sigma^2(v_j)=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\left(v_j-\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^Mv_j\right)^2$ and finite population covariance $\sigma(v_j,w_j)=\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^M\left(v_j-\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^Mv_j\right)\left(w_j-\frac1M\sum_{j=1}^Mw_j\right)$.'

(S6) Reading used throughout, implicit in the paper and not printed in these words: 'randomly assigned' means that every set $J_1$ of $m_t$ of the $M$ clusters is equally likely (complete randomization of clusters); $\mathrm{E}$, $\mathrm{V}$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ of estimators are taken over that distribution with the potential outcomes and cluster sizes fixed; $N=\sum_{j=1}^Mn_j$ and every $n_j\geq1$. $Y_{ij}$ denotes the observed outcome of individual $i$ in cluster $j$. In Appendix C (p. 72, PDF p. 34) the paper also writes $\mathrm{E}[\cdot]$ and an overline for the average over the $M$ clusters of a cluster-indexed quantity, and writes the cluster totals as $Y^T_{j0},Y^T_{j1}$ where the main text writes $Y^T_{0j},Y^T_{1j}$. The paper has no numbered theorems; its results are numbered equations.

canonical_claim.statement:
Printed statement refuted: equation (31) as printed, $\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}}{N}\right]=\Delta+\frac MN(\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{cj}})-\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{cj}}))$, whose right-hand side equals $\Delta$ for every $\hat k$.

Counterexample (validator, exact). $M=3$, $m_t=1$, $m_c=2$, $(n_1,n_2,n_3)=(1,2,3)$, $N=6$, $(Y^T_{01},Y^T_{02},Y^T_{03})=(0,0,0)$, $(Y^T_{11},Y^T_{12},Y^T_{13})=(0,0,3)$, so $\Delta=1/2$. Let $\hat k$ be the ordinary least squares slope of the observed cluster totals $Y^T_j$ on $n_j$ (with an intercept and no treatment indicator) over the three clusters, i.e. $\hat k=\sigma(n_j,Y^T_j)/\sigma^2(n_j)$ computed from the observed totals. Over the three equally likely assignments (treated cluster 1, 2, 3):
$\hat k=(0,0,3/2)$; $\overline{n_{tj}}=(1,2,3)$; $\overline{n_{cj}}=(5/2,2,3/2)$; $\frac1N\left[\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}\right]=(0,0,3/8)$ with $\hat k$ in place of $k$ in equations 20 and 21.
Hence $\mathrm{E}\left[\frac{\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}}{N}\right]=\frac18\neq\frac12=\Delta$: the bias is $-\frac38$, not $0$. Moreover $\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{tj}})=\frac12$, $\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{cj}})=-\frac14$ and $\frac MN\left(\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{cj}})-\mathrm{Cov}(\hat k,\overline{n_{tj}})\right)=\frac12\left(-\frac14-\frac12\right)=-\frac38$, in agreement with the corrected equation (31).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Des Raj difference estimator, equations (20)-(21) and the display after (22), p. 54 (PDF p. 16): $\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}=\frac M{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}=\frac M{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}=\frac1N\left[\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}\right]$, with $k$ a constant fixed before analysis; differenced variable $U^T_j=Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M)$ (p. 54), with potential versions $U^T_{0j}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ and $U^T_{1j}=Y^T_{1j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ (used on pp. 55-56; the first display of Section 5.3, p. 56, shows $U^T_{0j}-\overline{U^T_{0j}}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)-\overline{Y^T_{0j}}$). Finite population variance and covariance with divisor $M$, p. 50 (PDF p. 12) (standing assumption S5). $\hat k$, $\overline{n_{tj}}$, $\overline{n_{cj}}$: p. 58 (PDF p. 20) and p. 71 (PDF p. 33), as in the corrected-statement target for this finding.
canonical_claim.note: Finding rated Minor (error). The instance is the validator's (derivations.md, section E005; checks-output.json, key E005: slopes (0, 0, 1.5), estimates (0, 0, 0.375), ATE 0.5, bias -0.375, corrected covariance bias -0.375, printed covariance bias 0). It also exhibits the headline statement that estimating k from the same data can lead to bias (footnote 8, p. 54).

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 5.2, equations (24)-(25): invariance of the Des Raj difference estimator
canonical_claim.location: pp. 55-56 (PDF pp. 17-18); transformation defined on p. 49 (PDF p. 11)
canonical_claim.statement:
Setting (p. 49): '$Y^*_{1ij}\equiv b_0+b_1\cdot Y_{1ij}$ and likewise, the control outcomes, $Y^*_{0ij}\equiv b_0+b_1\cdot Y_{0ij}$.' p. 55: 'Since $k$ is on the same scale as the outcome variable, when the outcome variable is transformed, $k$ will also be transformed: $k^*=(b_0+b_1\cdot k).$ (24) Using this new $k^*$, we may again define new differenced treatment outcomes, $U^{T*}_{1j}=Y^{T*}_{1j}-k^*\cdot(n_j-N/M)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}(b_0+b_1\cdot Y_{1ij})-(b_0+b_1\cdot k)\cdot(n_j-N/M)=n_j\cdot b_0+b_1\cdot Y^T_{1j}-(b_0+b_1\cdot k)\cdot(n_j-N/M)=b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{1j}.$' p. 56: 'And, likewise, we may define new differenced control outcomes, $U^{T*}_{0j}=b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{0j}$. The estimate based on these transformed variables will be
$\widehat{\Delta^*_{R1}}=\frac MN\left[\frac1{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}U^{T*}_j-\frac1{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}U^{T*}_j\right]$
$=\frac MN\left[\frac1{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}(b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{1j})-\frac1{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}(b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{0j})\right]$ [corrected line: the paper prints $U^T_{1j}$ in the sum over $j\in J_0$]
$=\frac MN\left[\frac1{m_t}b_1\sum_{j\in J_1}U^T_{1j}-\frac1{m_c}b_1\sum_{j\in J_0}U^T_{0j}\right]$
$=b_1\cdot\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}.$ (25)
The Des Raj estimator is therefore invariant to linear transformation because any linear transformation to the outcome will necessarily be reflected in $k$.'

Corrected statement, with every hypothesis. For all cluster sizes $n_j\geq1$ with $N=\sum_jn_j$, all individual potential outcomes, all real $b_0,b_1,k$, and every assignment with $|J_1|=m_t$, $|J_0|=m_c$, $0<m_t<M$: with $U^T_{1j}=Y^T_{1j}-k(n_j-N/M)$, $U^T_{0j}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)$, $Y^{T*}_{1j}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}Y^*_{1ij}$, $Y^{T*}_{0j}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}Y^*_{0ij}$, $k^*=b_0+b_1k$, $U^{T*}_{1j}=Y^{T*}_{1j}-k^*(n_j-N/M)$, $U^{T*}_{0j}=Y^{T*}_{0j}-k^*(n_j-N/M)$ and $U^{T*}_j$ the observed one ($U^{T*}_{1j}$ for $j\in J_1$, $U^{T*}_{0j}$ for $j\in J_0$), one has $U^{T*}_{1j}=b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{1j}$, $U^{T*}_{0j}=b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{0j}$, every equality of the corrected chain (25) holds, and $\widehat{\Delta^*_{R1}}=b_1\cdot\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Des Raj difference estimator, equations (20)-(21) and the display after (22), p. 54 (PDF p. 16): $\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}=\frac M{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}=\frac M{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}=\frac1N\left[\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}\right]$, with $k$ a constant fixed before analysis; differenced variable $U^T_j=Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M)$ (p. 54), with potential versions $U^T_{0j}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ and $U^T_{1j}=Y^T_{1j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ (used on pp. 55-56; the first display of Section 5.3, p. 56, shows $U^T_{0j}-\overline{U^T_{0j}}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)-\overline{Y^T_{0j}}$). Invariance: p. 49 (PDF p. 11), equation (14), 'Invariance to this transformation would imply that ... $\widehat{\Delta^*_{HT}}=b_1\cdot\widehat{\Delta_{HT}}$'. $\widehat{\Delta^*_{R1}}$ is the Des Raj estimator computed from the transformed outcomes $Y^*$ with $k^*$ in place of $k$.
canonical_claim.note: Finding P020-E010 rated Minor (error), slip (e): the second line of (25) has the treatment subscript in the control sum. All other lines are as printed. This target is also the location-invariance part of headline claim H6. Another slip of the same finding on p. 55, read as corrected: 'the same transformation must be applied to k as to $Y^T_{0ij}$ and $Y^T_{1ij}$' should name the individual outcomes $Y_{0ij}$, $Y_{1ij}$ (no total superscript). The covariate version (p. 59, PDF p. 21) is stated in prose only: 'as long as $k'$ undergoes the same linear transformation as the original data and $k_a$ ($\forall a\in A$) undergoes the same multiplicative scale shift, the Des Raj estimator with covariates will also be invariant'. Derivation: derivations.md, section E010.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix C, equations (33)-(35) and the sentence that introduces them
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed (p. 72): 'Now note that the terms $\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})$, $\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})$, and $\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})$ in equation 32 can be written as follows: ... (33) ... (34) and, defining $\delta_j=(n_j-N/M)$, $\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})=\mathrm{E}[U^T_{j0}U^T_{j1}]-\overline{U^T_0}\,\overline{U^T_1}=\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}-k\delta_j](Y^T_{j1}-k\delta_j)-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}=\ldots$ (35), respectively.'

Corrected statement, with every hypothesis. Let $k$ be a real constant, $\delta_j=(n_j-N/M)$, $U^T_{j0}=Y^T_{j0}-k\delta_j$ and $U^T_{j1}=Y^T_{j1}-k\delta_j$ for $j=1,\ldots,M$, with $N=\sum_jn_j$; let $\mathrm{E}[\cdot]$ denote the average over the $M$ clusters $j$ and an overline the cluster mean, and $\sigma^2$, $\sigma$ the finite population variance and covariance (divisor $M$). Then the terms $\sigma^2(U^T_{j1})$, $\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})$, and $\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})$ in equation 32 can be written as follows:
$\sigma^2(U^T_{j1})=\sigma^2(Y^T_{j1})+k^2\sigma^2(n_j)-2k\sigma(Y^T_{j1},n_j),$ (33)
$\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})=\sigma^2(Y^T_{j0})+k^2\sigma^2(n_j)-2k\sigma(Y^T_{j0},n_j),$ (34)
and
$\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})=\mathrm{E}[U^T_{j0}U^T_{j1}]-\overline{U^T_0}\,\overline{U^T_1}$
$=\mathrm{E}[(Y^T_{j0}-k\delta_j)(Y^T_{j1}-k\delta_j)]-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}$ [corrected line: the paper closes the expectation bracket after the first factor]
$=\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}Y^T_{j1}-Y^T_{j0}k\delta_j-Y^T_{j1}k\delta_j+k^2\delta_j^2]-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}$
$=\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}Y^T_{j1}]-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}-\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}k\delta_j]-\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j1}k\delta_j]+\mathrm{E}[k^2\delta_j^2]$
$=\sigma(Y^T_{j0},Y^T_{j1})-k[\sigma(Y^T_{j0},n_j)+\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}]\mathrm{E}[\delta_j]]-k[\sigma(Y^T_{j1},n_j)+\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j1}]\mathrm{E}[\delta_j]]+k^2\sigma^2(n_j)$
$=\sigma(Y^T_{j0},Y^T_{j1})-k[\sigma(Y^T_{j0},n_j)+\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}]\cdot0]-k[\sigma(Y^T_{j1},n_j)+\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j1}]\cdot0]+k^2\sigma^2(n_j)$
$=\sigma(Y^T_{j0},Y^T_{j1})-k\sigma(Y^T_{j0},n_j)-k\sigma(Y^T_{j1},n_j)+k^2\sigma^2(n_j),$ (35)
respectively.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Equation (32), p. 71 (PDF p. 33): '$v\mathrm{V}(\widehat{\Delta_{R1}})=c\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})+t\sigma^2(U^T_{j1})+2\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})$ (32) where $v=\frac{(M-1)N^2}{M^2}$, $c=\frac{M-m_c}{m_c}$, and $t=\frac{M-m_t}{m_t}$' (p. 72). $\delta_j=(n_j-N/M)$ (p. 72). Finite population variance and covariance with divisor $M$, p. 50 (PDF p. 12) (standing assumption S5). In Appendix C, $Y^T_{j0}$, $Y^T_{j1}$, $U^T_{j0}$, $U^T_{j1}$ are the main text's $Y^T_{0j}$, $Y^T_{1j}$, $U^T_{0j}$, $U^T_{1j}$; $\mathrm{E}[\cdot]$ is the average over clusters, e.g. $\mathrm{E}[\delta_j]=\frac1M\sum_j\delta_j=0$; $\overline{Y^T_0}=\frac1M\sum_jY^T_{j0}$, $\overline{Y^T_1}=\frac1M\sum_jY^T_{j1}$, $\overline{U^T_0}$, $\overline{U^T_1}$ likewise (so $\overline{U^T_0}=\overline{Y^T_0}$ and $\overline{U^T_1}=\overline{Y^T_1}$).
canonical_claim.note: Finding P020-E010 rated Minor (error), slips (h) and (i): the introductory list repeats $\sigma^2(U^T_{j0})$ where $\sigma^2(U^T_{j1})$ is required (the validator fixes the first entry so that the list matches (33), (34), (35) 'respectively'), and the second line of the (35) display closes the expectation bracket before the second factor. Equations (33) and (34) and the remaining lines of (35) are as printed. The validator records that the index order j0/j1 in Appendix C is a harmless relabeling. These expansions are the finite identities behind headline claim H7. Derivation: derivations.md, section E010.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Equation (25), second line as printed; equation (35) display, second line as printed
canonical_claim.statement:
Two printed intermediate lines refuted by explicit instances (validator).

(a) Equation (25), second line as printed: $\frac MN\left[\frac1{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}(b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{1j})-\frac1{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}(b_0\cdot N/M+b_1\cdot U^T_{1j})\right]$, asserted equal to $\widehat{\Delta^*_{R1}}=\frac MN\left[\frac1{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}U^{T*}_j-\frac1{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}U^{T*}_j\right]$. Instance: $M=2$, $m_t=m_c=1$, $(n_1,n_2)=(1,2)$, $N=3$, $(Y^T_{01},Y^T_{02})=(0,0)$, $(Y^T_{11},Y^T_{12})=(1,2)$, $k=0$, $b_0=0$, $b_1=1$, cluster 1 treated ($J_1=\{1\}$, $J_0=\{2\}$). Then $U^T_{1j}=Y^T_{1j}$, $U^T_{0j}=Y^T_{0j}$, $U^{T*}_j=U^T_j$, and $\widehat{\Delta^*_{R1}}=\frac23[1-0]=\frac23=b_1\cdot\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}$, whereas the printed second line equals $\frac23[U^T_{11}-U^T_{12}]=\frac23[1-2]=-\frac23$.

(b) Equation (35) display, second line as printed: $\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}-k\delta_j](Y^T_{j1}-k\delta_j)-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}$, asserted equal to $\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})$. Instance: $M=2$, control totals of clusters 1 and 2 equal to $(0,2)$, treatment totals equal to $(0,2)$, $k=0$ (cluster sizes are then immaterial; for definiteness $(n_1,n_2)=(1,2)$). Then $\sigma(U^T_{j0},U^T_{j1})=\mathrm{E}[Y^T_{j0}Y^T_{j1}]-\overline{Y^T_0}\,\overline{Y^T_1}=2-1=1$, whereas the printed expression equals $1\cdot Y^T_{j1}-1$, which depends on $j$ and takes the value $-1$ at $j=1$ (and $1$ at $j=2$).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Des Raj difference estimator, equations (20)-(21) and the display after (22), p. 54 (PDF p. 16): $\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}=\frac M{m_c}\sum_{j\in J_0}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}=\frac M{m_t}\sum_{j\in J_1}(Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M))$, $\widehat{\Delta_{R1}}=\frac1N\left[\widehat{Y^T_{1,R1}}-\widehat{Y^T_{0,R1}}\right]$, with $k$ a constant fixed before analysis; differenced variable $U^T_j=Y^T_j-k(n_j-N/M)$ (p. 54), with potential versions $U^T_{0j}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ and $U^T_{1j}=Y^T_{1j}-k(n_j-N/M)$ (used on pp. 55-56; the first display of Section 5.3, p. 56, shows $U^T_{0j}-\overline{U^T_{0j}}=Y^T_{0j}-k(n_j-N/M)-\overline{Y^T_{0j}}$). Appendix C notation ($\mathrm{E}[\cdot]$ as the average over clusters, overlines as cluster means, $\delta_j=(n_j-N/M)$): p. 72 (PDF p. 34). Transformed quantities $U^{T*}$, $k^*$: pp. 55-56 (PDF pp. 17-18).

Instances from derivations.md, section E010, and checks-output.json (keys E010_control_subscript: correct 0.6667, printed intermediate -0.6667; E010_bracket: correct covariance 1.0, printed expression by cluster (-1.0, 1.0)). canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 4.2, the 'two important facts' under the sharp null and the display for $\mathrm{V}^N(\widehat{\Delta_{HT}})$ (unnumbered)
canonical_claim.statement:
As printed (pp. 51-52): 'One common sharp null hypothesis is that of the sharp null hypothesis of no treatment effect: $H_0:\tau_i=0,\ \forall i$. $H_0$ implies that the treatment has no effect whatsoever on the outcome, i.e. that both potential outcomes are identical: $Y_0i=Y_{1i}=Y_i$. When the sharp null hypothesis of no effect holds, we know two important facts: $\sigma^2(Y_{0j})=\sigma^2(Y_{1j})=\sigma^2(Y_j)$ and $\sigma(Y_{0j},Y_{1j})=\sigma^2(Y_j)$. By substituting $\sigma^2$ into the last line of equation 17, we may calculate the true variance under this null hypothesis, $\mathrm{V}^N(\widehat{\Delta_{HT}})=\frac{M^2}{N^2}\left[\frac M{M-1}\left[\frac{\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{m_c}+\frac{\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{m_t}\right]+\frac1{M-1}[2\sigma^2(Y^T_j)-\sigma^2(Y^T_j)-\sigma^2(Y^T_j)]\right]=\frac{M^4\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{N^2(M-1)m_cm_t}.$ Note that if the sharp null hypothesis of no effect holds, $\mathrm{V}^N(\widehat{\Delta_{HT}})$ is the true variance, which can be calculated from the data exactly or by way of resampling.'

Corrected statement, with every hypothesis (validator's repair: $Y_{0i}=Y_{1i}=Y_i$, and the total superscript restored in the two facts). Under random allocation of $m_t$ of the $M$ clusters to treatment ($0<m_t<M$, $m_c=M-m_t$), suppose $H_0:\tau_i=0\ \forall i$ holds, i.e. $Y_{0i}=Y_{1i}=Y_i$ for every individual. Then $Y^T_{0j}=Y^T_{1j}=Y^T_j$ for every cluster $j$ and every assignment, and
$\sigma^2(Y^T_{0j})=\sigma^2(Y^T_{1j})=\sigma^2(Y^T_j)$ and $\sigma(Y^T_{0j},Y^T_{1j})=\sigma^2(Y^T_j)$;
substituting into the last line of equation 17,
$\mathrm{V}(\widehat{\Delta_{HT}})=\mathrm{V}^N(\widehat{\Delta_{HT}})=\frac{M^2}{N^2}\left[\frac M{M-1}\left[\frac{\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{m_c}+\frac{\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{m_t}\right]+\frac1{M-1}[2\sigma^2(Y^T_j)-\sigma^2(Y^T_j)-\sigma^2(Y^T_j)]\right]=\frac{M^4\sigma^2(Y^T_j)}{N^2(M-1)m_cm_t},$
where $\sigma^2(Y^T_j)$ is the finite population variance of the observed cluster totals, which under $H_0$ is the same for every assignment.
